about: Every committed artefact a join must RE-DERIVE on the joined tree rather than take from either side (doc/claude/JOINING.md § The script). `paths` are whole files that are nothing but the artefact: a conflict in one is resolved to either side and re-derived, and a commit touching only such files is skipped by `scripts/join.py`. `inputs` are the paths whose change makes re-deriving necessary. `pin` names a file of numbers that must not GROW: a rise is accepted only up to the growth each source pinned on its own tree. `regen` runs in order; `check` must pass afterwards. `union_files` are append-only (a conflict keeps both sides); `shrink_files` are ratchets that only lose lines (a conflict keeps the lines BOTH sides still carry). `row_files` are hand-written docs holding measured `| **N** |` rows: a commit that changes only such rows there is not missing for that file. `ci: true` marks an artefact that is a pure function of the tree — no pin, no judgement — which `.github/workflows/derive.yml` regenerates on a runner and commits back (`scripts/derive_ci.py` runs exactly those, in this order); a ratchet never carries it. A `paths` entry may be a glob (`doc/lib-*.html`).

artefacts.name: compiled-stdlib
artefacts.note: the stdlib's compiled loft bodies (@PLN181): stale after any default/*.loft change, and a stale one is interpreted 5-23x slower — first, because the census and the allocation pins measure the build it produces

artefacts.name: optional-ratchet
artefacts.cure: peel the new shape tests with `.base()` (@FR-N-Shape) — a growth is a code change, never a re-pin

artefacts.name: frontend-allocations
artefacts.cure: two pins: the `stdlib` row is the COLD stdlib parse, and a new default/ declaration also moves the `tiny`/`medium` program rows by one constant (the scope pass and lints read every definition each run) — accept that with --accept frontend-allocations and name the declarations in the commit; a program delta that grows with the corpus is the front end: find the new allocation (tests/frontend_counts.rs reports both halves and says which applies). PERFORMANCE.md § Front-end speed
artefacts.note: pinned from the counts the advisory CI job `front-end allocation pins (ubuntu, advisory)` publishes — the runner reads more on the program rows than a development box, so a local re-pin would lower them; a join leaves the file to that job

artefacts.name: rewrite-census
artefacts.cure: a DROP is a rewrite that stopped firing on the union: find the condition that tightened, or bless it by hand as a deliberate decline

artefacts.name: browser-bundle
artefacts.note: rebuilt only when its source stamp moved (scripts/wasm_bundle_stamp.sh): its bytes depend on the toolchain, so an unconditional rebuild re-commits ~9 MB of wasm on every runner pass with no source change

artefacts.name: sprite-pack
regen: cd tools/brick-buster && ../../target/release/loft --interpret check_pack.loft >/dev/null 2>&1 || { ../../target/release/loft --interpret pack_atlas.loft >/dev/null && cp assets/bb.meta.store assets/bb.blobs.store assets/bb.meta.store.dschema assets/bb.blobs.store.dschema ../../doc/assets/; }
artefacts.note: the gallery's Brick Buster sprite pack: stored records, so a layout rule that moves a field leaves it unreadable and the page draws nothing (loft#1956). Rebuilt only when check_pack.loft refuses it: the packer does not write byte-identical output twice

artefacts.name: docs-lint-baseline
artefacts.note: a REPORT baseline re-pinned at release, never on a join: its committed counts lag every branch, and the PR's own `make docs-lint-gate` judges what a branch adds.  Registered so a conflict in it resolves to either side.

artefacts.name: ownership-drop-gate
artefacts.cure: a NEW line is a cell that releases wrongly on the union: fix it; only GONE lines (fixes) may be blessed, by hand

artefacts.name: reference-pages
artefacts.note: the reference pages gendoc writes, with the library pages rendered from the published packages `make doc` fetches — a box without them keeps the committed pages, so the runner (a clean cache, the registry reachable) is the reliable writer
